synthesis.headline: No. Twenty-nine days after the objective was frozen, the only engine that has audited real code is a one-file, one-attempt, tool-less LLM read whose measured root-location recall is 9-13% per pass on the repo's own planted corpus (both real-run Highs were single-file false positives that two reviewers supported), while the seven-pass pipeline that could plausibly be firm-grade cannot make a single real model call from any user command and has never run outside a fake provider. Velocity is high (49 tickets closed, ~245k lines of product code, 1,558 worklog entries) but it has moved zero goal-defining requirements: the loop optimises for refusal surface and record custody, defines COMPLETE by passing-test counts, cannot represent success in its own schemas, and keeps the human as scheduler, executor and sole feedback channel. The architecture is the right shape for "no model self-qualifies"; it is currently the wrong priority for "best auditor", and it is not integrated anywhere a user could obtain it.
synthesis.distance_to_goal:
DONE (verified working, category 1): an fcntl-locked atomic cost ledger with a hard $250 cap that held in the real run (cost_ledger.py:488-1023); in-memory secret transport with no ambient key reads (operator_secrets.py:110-190); per-response model/provider/endpoint identity validation that correctly refused OpenRouter's duplicate glm-5.2 routes (openrouter.py:25503-25611); strict-mypy-green typed artifacts over 341 modules; a sound consensus ladder, 22-role specialist catalogue, per-surface review records and a firm-grade CandidateFinding schema on the product path (consensus.py:381-441; schemas.py:2803-2826, 3474-3486); a documentary lineage manifest that groups cogito under the DeepSeek root and a tested same-root predicate (evidence_seal_authority.py:148); a request-blinded 24-case corpus with provenance pins; sandbox-exec isolation preflight passing on macOS; and a development ensemble that completed 125/125 ForestRoadVault files for ~$33 settled while honestly labelling every artifact non-qualifying.

NOT DONE, in critical-path order: (1) no user-runnable command executes an audit with a real model through the firm-grade design — `mmaudit run` fails closed at pipeline.py:4093-4098 and the only authority issuers are test-only, so completed_real_audits is 0 and detection quality of the product design is unmeasured; (2) no ground truth that can measure firm-grade detection — 13 KB of synthetic excerpts scored by exact line/keyword match, the public origin refused by code, and the 28-case product benchmark leaking its labels as `// BENCHMARK:` comments; (3) no cross-file context on realistic contracts — CALL_CLOSED is unreachable for any contract with a mapping, internal call or off-tree interface call, so automatic partitioning refuses real protocols and the model still sees one file or the whole bundle; (4) no deterministic detection lineage on by default — compile, Slither, formal, invariants and the target's own test suite are all off or unwired, and the default `mmaudit scan` yields zero Solidity findings; (5) no reviewer independence, insufficient-context state or severity calibration where findings are actually decided; (6) no engagement gate, no N-pass union, no provider rotation — an 18-token empty response is a clean SUCCESS and identical requests at temperature 0 share a median of one located root; (7) no in-run retry, ledger settlement/release, parallelism or typed refusal codes — every 429 or killed call is a human re-invocation and phantom accounting consumed $54 of one $83 ledger; (8) a PoC DSL that cannot deploy an attacker contract, so CONFIRMED is unreachable for reentrancy/flash-loan/callback/signature exploits, plus macOS-only fork execution and operator-pinned targets; (9) governance that cannot express Done (completed_real_audits le=0, unsatisfied gates ge=1, 721 Literal[False] authorities), `make test` that does not collect, CI that only runs by hand, main frozen at the day before the goal, and five days of product code uncommitted; (10) no seal issuer and no external anchor — the "transparency proof" is a local Merkle prefix and the OTS client is unreachable from any command.

Spend to date: ~$46 actual / ~$110 accounted across all ledgers, $0.45 actual on the qualified path (one 24-case campaign attempt on 08-27, failed closed at $0.20, never retried). Rough order of remaining work: make one engine executable end to end (1) and give it a corpus it can be measured on (2) — nothing downstream can be evaluated until both exist; then win detection quality with context closure, the deterministic layer, reviewer independence and engagement/union (3-6); then make it unattended and confirmable with resilience and the PoC DSL (7-8); then make it a product with representable Done, green CI and a committed tree (9); then make it authoritative with a real seal (10). Items 9's hygiene subset (two __init__.py files, a commit, push-triggered CI) is cheap and should be done immediately as the precondition for an autonomous builder to do 3-8 safely.

surviving_findings.finding: The product audit path (`mmaudit run`) cannot execute a model. The only AuditPipeline constructor in src/ passes none of the six live authorities the pipeline demands; with an API key present the run raises before any provider call, without one it terminates MODEL_FAILURE. The only issuers of those authorities are called solely from tests, and their prerequisite VerifiedProductionQualification is unobtainable because the persisted loader ends in an unconditional raise and `models qualify`/`verify-qualification` hardcode trusted_campaign_verification = None, making every candidate INCONCLUSIVE. The seven-pass design (blind shards, specialists, verifier, cross-examination, falsifier, judge) has therefore only ever run under FakeOpenRouter (MOCK) and every model-driven test asserts INCOMPLETE. A separate `mmaudit development` sub-app does reach real models but bypasses this pipeline entirely and is self-labelled non-qualifying.

surviving_findings.finding: The only engine path that has audited real code is the development corpus/ensemble: one to three tool-less, single-turn LLM reads per primary file (candidate plus up to two reviewers) with no compilation, static analysis or execution, a thin finding schema (no preconditions, attack path, evidence, reachability, false-positive conditions or confidence), a 5-class-plus-other taxonomy and a 16-finding cap per shard. Its only nontrivial measured quality, on the repo's own 19-file/45-root planted corpus, is 4-6/45 root location per trial (8.9-13.3%), 15/45 union over five temperature-0 trials with a median pairwise overlap of one root, pooled structural precision 26/295 = 8.8%, category agreement with labels 0 of 8, and 1 of 12 located roots stable across two identical passes. On ForestRoadVault it produced 317 claims, 0 Highs reaching consensus, and both Highs were refuted by code one file away. No competitor baseline exists in the tree; 'far below any firm' is an inference from the absolute numbers.

Either fold it into the product pipeline as an 'unqualified' profile that shares the CandidateFinding schema, compile and scanner evidence, or retire it to smoke/benchmark duty once F1 lands. surviving_findings.finding: There is no runnable tree-in/report-out path, and cross-file context is structurally unavailable. The new dependency-closure module builds its index with empty artifact roots, so every graph edge is HEURISTIC at confidence 0.4/0.55 against a policy pinned at exactly 0.9 that also requires COMPILER or STATIC_TOOL provenance; CALL_CLOSED is therefore reachable only when the heuristic graph emits zero facts. A `mapping` declaration is refused as UNSUPPORTED_TYPE with global scope, poisoning every primary in the tree. Reproduced offline: a 7-line vault → NOT_ESTABLISHED; the real ForestRoadVault tree (81 files) raises a work-ceiling ValueError and only 13 import-free interface/constant files ever close. Tree planning refuses any non-CALL_CLOSED primary and run-tree-plan refuses unless READY, so the operator hand-built 125 one-file manifests. Without a partition every source is a primary and every request renders every file. Nothing renders ensemble output into a report. DEPCLOSURE was marked COMPLETE on 3,322 passing test identities using a fixture whose positive control has zero graph facts; AUTOPARTITION's 256-primary acceptance ran on a mock transport with 4M-12M-token prompt limits, $1e-9 prices and a one-function abstract contract. All closure/partition/tree modules are untracked.

surviving_findings.finding: Cross-lineage consensus — the goal's core authority mechanism — is a same-answer filter with no lineage concept on any path that decides findings. Development path: both reviewers receive exactly the candidate's context and are asked whether 'the claim as written' is supported, so conditional or self-caveated claims pass; the verdict space is SUPPORTED/REFUTED/INCONCLUSIVE with no 'depends on unsupplied code' state; consensus is unanimity-or-INCONCLUSIVE with disagreement only counted; reviewer distinctness is exact-model-id/canonical-slug set disjointness; lineage_independence is a single-valued Literal NOT_ESTABLISHED on all 14 development artifact types; the candidate model actually used (z-ai/glm-5.3) is absent from the lineage manifest and its reviewer 2 (z-ai/glm-5.2) belongs to a family the manifest itself constrains as non-independent. In the real run 37 of 68 claims whose own text said a dependency was not supplied were SUPPORTED by both reviewers. Product path: root_lineage is an operator-typed sha256 literal in TOML never cross-checked against the manifest; cluster independence is a regex over the model-ID string; the two cross-examiners must differ from each other but are never compared to the candidate's origin, which CandidateFinding cannot even record; falsifier selection takes only config. The real same-root predicate exists only on the AUTHRUNNER benchmark path.

surviving_findings.why_it_matters_for_the_goal: Goal §2 clause 2 and guardrail 7a ('same-root judgement voids it') are enforced nowhere a finding is decided, and 'two reviewers agreed' means two model IDs read the same truncated text — this is neither false-positive control nor independence, and it is the ensemble's only potential edge over a single human reviewer.
surviving_findings.fix: Add a deterministic pre-review filter routing any claim that references an unsupplied symbol/file to INSUFFICIENT_CONTEXT; give reviewers the closure members of the primary; require at least one reviewer to receive a different context slice; on split opinions dispatch context expansion (fetch dependency, run test) and a third-lineage judge instead of INCONCLUSIVE. surviving_findings.finding: Severity is never calibrated downward by any automated step. On the development path the candidate model's severity is published verbatim (reviewers return only a verdict; no dedup, no reporting consumer). On the product path the published severity is max(highest-severity primary candidate, judge severity), so the judge can only raise it — designed and test-locked; the verifier schema has no severity field; post-merge caps lower only status. The sole downgrade mechanism is the operator-authored actor model, off by default.

surviving_findings.finding: The deterministic layer contributes nothing to Solidity detection by default. Formal, compile, invariant execution, Slither, Foundry/Hardhat fork and CodeQL are all disabled; the default-enabled Semgrep adapter ships three Python-only rules; Slither additionally requires operator solc version+sha pins; every formal engine requires operator version+sha pins; mutation kill scores are INCONCLUSIVE on every default path and the only crediting set is empty; no real engine SUCCESS artifact exists in the tree; targets are never derived from source. A default `mmaudit scan` of the full_protocol_offline fixture produced 0 findings and quality_status incomplete. The development path executes no tests at all, which is why the ensemble never noticed a remediation package had reversed a mandatory invariant (found only by a manual forge re-run). Kontrol can emit a bounded local PROOF from auto-derived properties (CP-04 refuted), but it is gated behind the same flags and pins.

surviving_findings.finding: The engine cannot tell a disengaged or provider-degraded model from a clean review, and provider rotation is manual by construction. A schema-valid empty findings list (~18 tokens) is recorded OBSERVED → NO_CANDIDATES and exits 0; the transport enforces only an upper completion-token bound; no engagement predicate exists anywhere in src/mmaudit and Codex declined to infer one. Every development request pins exactly one provider endpoint with fallbacks disabled, the audit path rejects more than one endpoint, and the client retries only the same route; no rotation or per-provider variance logic exists (measure-stability is benchmark-only and provider-blind). In the real run Together-hosted glm-5.3 returned an empty list in 18 tokens where others spent 13-21k and a 10-file pass was discarded by hand; the same model on four providers gave 1/2/4/5 claims on one file; the operator rotated providers by hand 8+ times.

surviving_findings.finding: The ground truth on which the goal's authority would be earned cannot measure firm-grade detection, and no admissible way to build a track record exists. The sealed corpus is 24 synthetic excerpts of 202-1,011 bytes (13,076 bytes total; the candidate sees only the excerpt) scored by exact classification, exact line-range equality and regex keyword-subset checks; the cross-lineage judge's per-dimension outcomes must equal the host rubric's own outcomes and be CONFIRMED or the seal is void, so the judge adds no independent signal. PUBLIC_ESTABLISHED ground truth is modelled but refused by the only resolver and excluded by the seal's compiled pin (case_count == 24, origin_kinds == SYNTHETIC_PLANTED only), so a public case would break the seal rather than extend it. The separate 28-case product benchmark (15 fixture files, 522 lines) hands the model its answer key: all 13 vulnerable cases leak — 12 via `// BENCHMARK: <bug>` comments and one via the contract name VulnerableInflationVault — and nothing strips them. Benchmark thresholds are pinned at 1.0/0.0 while measured single-pass recall on the development corpus is 9-13%. known_issue_taxonomy.v1.json is 19 defensive questions with finding_authority=false, not a vulnerability database.

surviving_findings.finding: Cost accounting and runtime shape turn every transient provider failure into a human re-invocation and every killed in-flight call into a ledger recreation. The development transport never retries and the CLI hardcodes maximum_attempts=1 at seven sites (also enforced by the models); a 429 with no billed cost is accounted UNCERTAIN_ACCOUNTED at the full estimate and permanently consumes the ceiling because the ledger has no generation-id field and no caller ever settles an uncertain row to a known cost; with --carry-uncertain-estimates such rows are carried, but a stranded RESERVED row from a killed call blocks all reservations and no CLI can release or settle a row, so the operator recreated the ledger twice, orphaning candidate observations that judgment requires byte-exact rows for. Ledger-5 shows $83.46 accounted against $29.37 settled. Shards execute strictly sequentially, halt at the first non-OBSERVED shard, and candidate plus two reviewers share one wall clock capped at 1800 s, so realistic manifests overrun in the reviewer legs; recovery is a separate human-invoked resume covering only the candidate stage. On the qualified AUTHRUNNER path the configured transient retry is dead by construction: finalize_active(None) raises OpenRouterCostControlError under an operator reservation before `continue`, and the next reservation is refused by require_known_prior_costs unless a human writes a byte-exact two-row legacy allowance into source.

surviving_findings.finding: Failures are undiagnosable to a supervisor. surviving_findings.finding: Integrity effort is concentrated on paths that do not decide findings. Custody, ledger and lineage machinery guard benchmark/release bookkeeping; in the audit pipeline the finding-status rule admits only one non-model signal — a local Foundry fork reproduction fingerprint that is ENVIRONMENT_BLOCKED on every Linux backend and cannot express attacker-contract exploits — while HIGH_CONFIDENCE is reachable from model verdicts alone and scanner evidence is discarded; independence there is a config-declared root_lineage string compared by set cardinality. surviving_findings.finding: The engineering shape fights an autonomous builder. The qualified core path is a single 9,928-line async method with 30 closures and 835 locals, and the provider client is a 10,951-line class with 4,437- and 2,131-line functions, exercised only end-to-end through fake clients and never against a real model (though the real-run operational fixes land in the 1-2k-line development modules, not these bodies). refuted_findings.claim: The dominant complexity in the codebase is in-process anti-tamper machinery (bytecode hashing of its own functions and of httpx/httpcore/h11 internals) defending against a threat model with no attacker, and it is the reason simple provider-behaviour changes are expensive.

(1) No bytecode hashing exists — zero co_code/marshal/hash-over-__code__ in src/mmaudit; the mechanism is `is`-identity on __code__/__closure__ objects captured at import (openrouter.py:5605-5660, :24639-24690) plus a version-string tuple. (2) 'Dominant' is unsupported: anti-tamper-named functions span 4.3% (narrow) to 7.0% (broad) of 426k lines; they dominate a few files (authenticated_runner.py 75%, runtime_evidence.py 59%) but not the codebase mass (models/ 162k, orchestration/ 116k; schemas.py 18.3k, pipeline.py 16.4k, scheduler.py 14.2k are not custody-heavy). (3) The causal claim is not shown: across 60 openrouter.py commits only 9.8% of added lines are seal-flavoured, sampled provider-behaviour commits (fd1459b, 5a675a1, 982abd7) added 0 lines inside any authority closure, and the concrete real-run fix (maximum_attempts=1) is a plain literal in development_cli.py, a file with zero seal tokens. The frozen goal also names an adversary — the process itself (§2 'no model self-qualifies enforced structurally') — so 'no attacker' contradicts the goal's framing. The growth-pattern observation survives in F19 via P7, which is scoped to what the loop optimises for, not to dominance or cost.

refuted_findings.claim: Formal proof of invariants is only reachable when an operator hand-writes a CVL spec and pays for Certora cloud; every local engine can only say 'counterexample' or 'none within bounds', and all of it is off by default and gated on operator-pinned deployed addresses.
refuted_findings.why_refuted: formal.py:2631 is not a docstring; it is the body of `_property_proof_evidence` (formal.py:2622-2634), which returns FormalResultKind.PROOF and is called from the Kontrol adapter's parse_result at formal.py:1466 for every property whose Kontrol outcome is passed/proved/verified/success. Kontrol is a local KEVM engine (`kontrol prove`, formal.py:1424-1445), registered in the default FormalRunner adapter list (:1660), run_kontrol defaults True (config.py:1244), listed in CERTIFIED_FORMAL_PROOF_ENGINES (assurance.py:178-180), and its input is auto-translated from the engine's own PropertyCorpus (engines/kontrol.py:41-59; properties.py:51), not a CVL spec — tests/unit/test_kontrol.py:250-255 asserts the PROOF emission. So PROOF has two emitters, one local and spec-free, and the proofs are explicitly bounded. The gating half (formal.enabled False, operator version+sha pins at formal.py:1355-1366, harness targets from config.reproduction.targets) is accurate and is carried in F7; the Certora-only, CVL-only, cloud-only mechanism is not.

strengths: The product-path finding schema and consensus ladder are firm-grade in design: CandidateFinding requires attack_path, preconditions, compensating_controls, false_positive_conditions, a verification_test and source/sink (schemas.py:2803-2826); CONFIRMED needs two exact VERIFIED verdicts plus a fork-reproduction fingerprint, HIGH_CONFIDENCE needs two VERIFIED plus a complete unguarded path, high/critical need two cross-examination decisions from two lineages (consensus.py:361-379, :381-441).

Per-surface review records with mandatory reachability paths (schemas.py:3474-3486, :3538-3572), a 22-role specialist catalogue with disjoint responsibilities (constants.py:47-70), anonymized cross-examination forbidden from inferring lineage (prompts/cross_examination.md:1-12), and anti-tautology PoC rules (exploit_test.md:11-13, :22-28) are stronger than most human reports' coverage and evidence discipline — if made executable.

The $250 ceiling is genuinely automated and fail-closed: an fcntl-locked atomic ledger with reserve → commit → reconcile, duplicate-id and over-cap refusal (cost_ledger.py:488-1023); the real engagement stayed at ~$90 accounted / ~$33 settled with no runaway, and gate-budget-ceiling is one of the three SATISFIED_AUTONOMOUS gates.

Secret transport meets goal §4 with no human in the loop (operator_secrets.py:110-190; no ambient os.environ key reads in src/), and per-response identity validation is sound and battle-tested — it correctly refused OpenRouter's duplicate exact routes for glm-5.2 in the real run (openrouter.py:25503-25611; operator_results.md:20-22).

Truthfulness is enforced in code, not prose: every development artifact hard-codes findings_validated/audit_complete/qualification_eligible/release_eligible False and labels output 'unvalidated defensive hypotheses'; MOCK/UNVERIFIED execution evidence cannot be credited; formal results distinguish 'no counterexample within bounds' from proof; the closure module refuses NOT_ESTABLISHED with 15 machine-readable shortfall codes rather than fabricating closure; NO_CANDIDATES/INCOMPLETE are never rendered as safe. First, it never ran the one product command a user can run against a realistic input; doing so offline shows the deterministic front half of the pipeline cannot ingest a standard Foundry+OpenZeppelin protocol for four independent reasons (lib/ not excluded and max_files truncation, remappings.txt dropped by include_docs=False, sharding refusal on a .DS_Store omission, and a profile-replay self-check that aborts the run on ERC-7201 constants) — an earlier and cheaper blocker than the authority chain that changes the shape of priority 1, and direct evidence that the integrity scaffolding it declined to indict does false-positive on real code. Second, it misreads the real run's two Highs: one was refuted, one was remediated, neither was two-reviewer-supported, and the evidence bundle said so; the ensemble's consensus step deserves credit it was denied. Third, it dropped map-level findings with customer and market consequences (open-weight-only model universe, EVM key/mnemonic redaction gap, Hardhat exclusion, the list-endpoints defect) and ignored the Cantina review and Slither report sitting in the target repo — the two cheapest external yardsticks for 'best in the world'. Fourth, it left ~55k lines of the product path (scheduler, context, truncation) unmapped while generalising development-path conclusions about context and engagement to the engine, and it attributes the refusal-surface growth to the builder without naming AGENTS.md:151-160 as the instruction that produces it. The priority order should add 'make `mmaudit scan` ingest a real Foundry tree' as item 1a, quantify L as roughly one smoke plus a $10-20 campaign away subject to the 4,096-token regime, and carry the AGENTS.md edit as the precondition for every process fix. With those corrections the synthesis's ordering and stop-doing list stand.
